items.title: Bulgaria's acting president Iliana Iotova leads presidential runoff, exit polls show
items.why: Iliana Iotova, Bulgaria's acting president since January, is ahead of the pro-Western former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov in Sunday's runoff. Parallel counts by polling agencies put her on about 57% to 58%, AFP and TRT World report. Turnout was under 30%.
items.matters: If confirmed, she would be Bulgaria's first elected woman president; she favours talks with Russia over the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Sweden's Andreas Almgren and Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui win New York City Marathon
items.why: Andreas Almgren won the men's race in 2 hours 6 minutes 1 second on his marathon debut, 13 seconds ahead of Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa. Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race in 2:24:36, six seconds ahead of the American Jess McClain.
items.matters: Almgren is the first Swedish runner to win one of the world's major marathons.

items.title: Golden State Valkyries win the WNBA title in only their second season
items.why: The Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in San Francisco on Saturday in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, 28 of them in the second half, and was named Finals MVP.
items.matters: It is the first title for the expansion team, which joined the league in 2025.

items.title: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta meeting without agreement on key issues
items.why: The two-day meeting of G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta, in the US, ended on Saturday without a joint statement, mainly because of divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, AP reports. The usual group photo was dropped after European and other ministers objected to posing with Russia's Sergey Lavrov.
items.matters: G20 leaders are due to meet in Florida in December; it is unclear whether Vladimir Putin will attend.

items.title: Iran orders 'unrestricted' response to any attack as Qatar pursues talks
items.why: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has told the armed forces to answer any attack with a 'geographically unrestricted response'. An Iranian delegation is in Doha for indirect talks through Qatari mediators. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says President Trump has not decided whether to resume strikes.
items.matters: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say more tankers hit mines in Hormuz; Qatar says one of its gas carriers was struck.

items.title: Youth-led protests spread across Europe as France marks a third weekend
items.why: France's interior ministry says about 320,000 people marched on Saturday over living costs, schools and housing, fewer than on the two previous weekends; police made more than 560 arrests, AP reports. Youth groups also rallied in more than 30 German cities, with looting in Frankfurt.
items.matters: Similar protests organised on social media have appeared in Italy, Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands in recent weeks.

items.title: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine through Belarus
items.why: Residents of Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, crossed into northern Ukraine from Belarus on Saturday after travelling through Russia, under a local ceasefire due to end on Sunday evening. Officials have not confirmed how many left; organisers said the convoy could carry more than 750 people.
items.matters: The White House says Melania Trump helped broker the truce; AP calls it the most significant since Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo pass 5,000
items.why: Congo's health ministry says the outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain, declared in May, has killed 5,026 people among 10,351 infections. Most cases are in the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain.
items.matters: It is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record; Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria have also reported cases.

items.changed: Updated: the FBI blames North Korean hackers, and withdrawals are restarting
items.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack
items.why: The FBI said on Saturday that North Korean hackers it tracks as 'TraderTraitor' stole more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, on about 29 October. Binance began restarting withdrawals in phases on Sunday and says customers will not bear the losses.
items.matters: It is the largest crypto theft on record; the FBI linked the same group to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025.
